title: You have a federal right to travel, to use public roads for private purposes, enjoyment of rights
summary: Tennessee blogger argues federal motor-carrier definitions show traffic laws reach only commerce, so private travelers can defeat tickets administratively.

assertions.quote: Transportation rules apply to people who have a calling or vocation in the business of using the roadways for hire and private profit and gain.
no wrong if you are not in commerce
If accused not in commerce, can cite federal protections

verdicts.note: FMCSA rules govern interstate carriers only; state traffic codes separately cover all drivers, and courts reject reading one through the other.
State traffic regulation of all motor vehicles is an independent exercise of state police power, so the reach of federal rules does not limit it.
States issue distinct non-commercial and commercial (CDL) licenses; an ordinary license confers no commercial status.
The law upheld required an operator's license of any person driving a motor vehicle on the highway, commercial or not.

assertions.quote: Traffic cases at heart are tax cases, privilege management civil claims and can be defeated on grounds of disregard of administrative rules.

verdicts.note: Traffic offences are prosecuted directly in court; administrative procedure acts do not require prior agency hearings for citations.

assertions.quote: Rules of the road so adopted apply only to residents

verdicts.note: Municipal traffic ordinances apply to anyone driving within city limits, resident or not.
